report:
## Report

The claim is well-supported by evidence — it is **true**, not false.

The pivotal RCT (Devinsky et al., NEJM 2017) randomized 120 children/young adults with Dravet syndrome to add-on cannabidiol (CBD, Epidiolex) or placebo. Median convulsive seizure frequency fell from 12.4 to 5.9 per month with CBD, versus 14.9 to 14.1 with placebo — a statistically significant reduction (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1611618). A subsequent dose-ranging phase 3 trial (JAMA Neurology, 2020) confirmed that both 10 mg/kg/day and 20 mg/kg/day CBD significantly reduced convulsive seizure frequency versus placebo in 199 children with Dravet syndrome (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379048758_The_efficacy_and_safety_of_cannabidiol_CBD_in_pediatric_patients_with_Dravet_Syndrome_a_narrative_review_of_clinical_trials).

FDA drug-trial data corroborate this: in the pivotal trial, nearly twice as many patients on 20 mg/kg/day CBD achieved a ≥75% reduction in convulsive seizures (23%) compared with placebo (12%) (https://www.epidiolex.com/epidiolex-results/dravet-syndrome; https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-approvals-and-databases/drug-trials-snapshots-epidiolex). These results led the FDA to approve Epidiolex (purified CBD) specifically for Dravet syndrome in 2018.

A 2020 systematic review and meta-analysis of the available RCTs (Lattanzi et al., CNS Drugs) further confirmed that adjunctive CBD significantly reduces seizure frequency and increases the proportion of ≥50% responders in Dravet syndrome, at the cost of increased somnolence, diarrhea, and liver enzyme elevations (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40263-020-00708-6).

**Conclusion:** Multiple randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials and meta-analyses consistently demonstrate that add-on CBD significantly reduces convulsive seizure frequency in children with Dravet syndrome. This evidence directly contradicts the premise that the claim is false — it is, in fact, robustly supported and underpinned the FDA approval of Epidiolex for this indication.
